mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) reflects stronger economic demand, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 35% of the time when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite UNRATE exceeding 8%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5%, it indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which should boost equity markets and lead to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weaker consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive despite a 5% YoY decline in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects stronger supply chains and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 35% of the time when INDPRO is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and exceeds 4%, it signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment (UNRATE) is high and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is declining, it signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive despite high UNRATE and declining PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it creates a scenario where real interest rates are negative, boosting equity markets and leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative despite low FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL.
